label: Entries in PostgreSQL
description: The same entries as @monitor/data/entries.store.json, kept in a database rather than in memory. Every word of the declaration is the same -- the collection, the shape, the key, what no two records may repeat, what an added column gives the rows already there -- and only the connection differs. Two stores exist because a profile swaps bindings and not connections (RFC 0002 settled that; RFC 0005 is where it changes), so this is the seam until it does.

entries.description: the observed calls, one row each: no two record the same call, a note is a field of the entry, and a row that predates the user agent column reads as unknown

latest.description: the most recent call recorded for each method, one row per method: written in the same transaction as the entry itself, so the two cannot disagree
